name: Sand Timer
summary: A working hourglass on a desk: flip it to start, lay it down to pause, and watch real grains pile up
about: An hourglass with a turned wooden frame stands on a desk by a window, and its sand is a real falling-sand simulation of about 1,700 grains, paced so the last grain lands exactly when 1, 3, 5 or 10 minutes are up. Flip it with a lift, a half turn and a bump, lay it on its side to pause or drag it to tilt the sand, and when time is up a bell rings and the desk glows. Good for a focus or study page, a cooking timer or a calm waiting screen.
how: Pick 1, 3, 5 or 10 minutes and press Flip: it lifts, turns over with a bounce and the sand starts to run.
Press Lay down to tip it on its side and pause the clock; press Stand up to carry on.
Drag the hourglass sideways (or use the left and right arrows) to tilt it and watch the sand slide; tap it to knock the grains.
When time is up a bell rings once you have tapped the page, sparkles fly and the note card says TIME.
The card on the desk and the caption show the time left; reduced motion keeps every step without the bounce.
